title: ArchMap is a web-based platform for reference-based analysis of single-cell datasets.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py: no PMCID, no full text, no supplement, no accessions, no NCBI links (GEO/SRA), no Zenodo/Dryad hits. archmap.bio returns a 670-byte single-page web app shell with no file listing. GitHub theislab/archmap is an MIT-licensed code repository (frontend, backend, mapping pipeline), not a data deposit. The ArchMap docs say mapping runs on scArches models, with KNN (k-nearest neighbours), XGBoost and scANVI/scPoli classifiers, and that logging in is optional.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the abstract and search snippets only: ArchMap hosts many published reference atlases, some of them Human Cell Atlas references, plus scvi-hub models. I did not enumerate atlas sizes, cell counts or label columns. My claim that atlas files run to several GB is general knowledge, not checked.

a1_downloadable.note: The paper deposits no dataset: Europe PMC, NCBI and Zenodo/Dryad show nothing. The web platform is a tool, and the atlases it uses belong to other papers and live on other sites such as CELLxGENE and scvi-hub (not checked).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: This paper releases no label. The only candidate label would be cell-type annotations in third-party atlases, which would mean picking and harmonizing labels across atlases, i.e. building the label.

a3_inputs_present.note: No feature table is released. Inputs would be expression matrices from third-party atlases (not checked).

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable: there is no released table to check.

a5_enough_rows.note: This paper releases no rows. Atlas cell counts were not checked.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; typical integrated atlases are multi-GB h5ad files (single-cell data files), not verified
a6_fits_laptop.note: Integrated reference atlases of millions of cells usually exceed the 5 GB limit. Not checked in the files.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing to compare: there is no full text and no files.

a8_label_provenance.note: Atlas cell-type labels are expert annotations, often made by clustering the same expression data or by earlier label transfer. Predicting them from expression is partly circular.

existing_models.name: scArches (with scVI/scANVI/scPoli), the mapping method behind ArchMap
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; the ArchMap docs have a 'Mapping evaluation' page that I did not open.

existing_models.name: CellTypist, a logistic-regression cell-type annotator with pretrained models
Azimuth, a reference-mapping tool
existing_models.score_and_split: Only a search snippet: a 2025 bioRxiv benchmark of Azimuth, CellTypist, scArches and FR-Match on lung atlases found accuracy varies, especially for rare cell types. Numbers not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Snippet only: annotating rare cell types.

backbone.name: scGPT / Geneformer (single-cell foundation models) or scArches-pretrained scVI models
backbone.hardware: CPU is possible for small subsets; a full atlas needs much more
backbone.licence: ArchMap code is MIT; each atlas has its own licence (not checked)

integration.partner_dataset: CELLxGENE Census (a large public single-cell collection)
integration.join_key: Ensembl gene IDs and Cell Ontology cell-type terms (not verified in the files)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does label transfer from a reference atlas hold up on query data from new labs, diseases or technologies? This is already a heavily benchmarked question.

controls.positive_control: Recover major lineages (immune vs epithelial) from marker genes.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the cell-type labels and confirm accuracy falls to the majority-class rate.
controls.external_validation: Hold out whole studies inside an atlas (not verified).

honest_claim_h3: At best, a model would predict cell types that expert curators gave to cells in a published atlas, on data like that atlas. This paper adds no new data to support that claim.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the gene expression of single cells to predict the cell type assigned to them in published reference atlases.
plain_idea.train_on: Gene-expression profiles of individual cells from third-party reference atlases. This paper releases no data, so the number of examples is unknown.
plain_idea.predict: The cell-type label that atlas curators assigned, often by clustering the same expression data, so the label is not an independent measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Little here is new: many open, benchmarked annotation tools already do this task, and ArchMap itself is one of them.

ml_idea: Reference-based cell-type label transfer. This task is saturated, and the paper is a software platform with no new dataset.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: the paper releases no dataset and I did not download any atlas.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Look for a data deposit from this paper. Europe PMC, NCBI and Zenodo/Dryad already showed none, so it is dead.

verdict_reason: This is a software and web-platform paper with no dataset deposited. The only usable labels are third-party atlas annotations, which are partly derived from the same expression data, and label transfer is already a crowded field with open tools (scArches, CellTypist, Azimuth).
